_comment: Joint declarations for check_collisions.py and motion_sweep.py. Part names are matched case-insensitively as substrings of each STL's basename, so 'bearing_608' matches 'build/bearing_608.stl'. Delete this _comment and replace the examples. The older bare-list form (contacts only, no motion) is still accepted.

contacts._comment: Declaring a pair licenses the interference you state -- not any interference. An overlap outside the range fails, and so does a declared press fit whose parts do not touch. Declared pairs are also exempt from the motion sweep, since they are meant to stay in contact. A pair within range is ALSO required to touch in exactly one contiguous region by default -- a legitimate contact plus an unrelated structural collision can otherwise hide behind the same declared range (INCIDENTS.md, 2026-08-19). Add "multi_region_ok": true only for a joint that genuinely touches in several places on purpose (e.g. a splined shaft) -- but that only bounds the COUNT of regions, not WHERE they are; for a stronger authorization, also declare "expected_bounds" (assembly-space bounding box every detected region must fall inside, added 2026-08-21). "derivation" is REQUIRED whenever expected_interference_mm is declared -- a non-empty trace back to the source parameters/formula this range came from, not a hand-typed guess (INCIDENTS.md, 2026-08-21).
contacts.derivation: bearing_608 OD 22.0mm nominal (catalogue), housing_bore modeled at 21.9mm -- 0.05-0.15mm radial interference per the shaft-fit table in references/hardware.md
lid and body share a nominal mating face at the same Z in layout.scad -- zero interference by construction, not measured

motion._comment: 'ratio' is this part's motion per unit of the sweep parameter. Meshing external gears turn OPPOSITE ways, so one ratio is negative -- getting that sign wrong is the easy mistake and produces a sweep that proves nothing. Give 'teeth' on every revolute driver and the sweep collapses to one tooth pitch; omit it to force the full range.
For a prismatic driver, 'ratio' is millimetres per unit of the sweep parameter, so range_deg [0, 100] with ratio 0.5 travels 50 mm.
